e8b_identity_reconciliation.summary_of_change: the pretrained identity now projects to 34.423 h with 0.577 h of headroom. Four separate omissions have now been found and corrected, every one of them UPWARD against an unchanged ceiling: the section-19 efficiency pass; the 10,004-row raw denominator with its raw-distribution pass and B1's intervention conditions; the retained parts of protocol 13.2b's A1 row; and the use of the low end rather than the maximum of the recorded per-epoch rates. The repeated direction of these corrections is itself the finding: each review has moved the number toward the ceiling, so the remaining margin should be treated as an upper bound on the true margin, not an estimate of it.

e8b_identity_reconciliation.verdict: FITS, but only just, and on assumptions that keep moving the wrong way: 34.423 h against the hard 35 h ceiling leaves 0.577 h, with a recorded retry allowance of NONE. The ceiling is NOT weakened and NOTHING was descoped -- every correction across four review rounds ADDED work. Five open risks are listed above and ANY ONE of them exhausts the remaining margin. This is now a decision for the user rather than a reassurance: either accept the risks explicitly, or close the largest of them with a short measurement before core execution is authorised.
e8b_identity_reconciliation.retry_allowance: NONE. The plan tolerates zero B3 retries; any retry or any additional B3-loading evaluation triggers a stop-and-ask BEFORE execution
residual_assumptions: CORRECTED 2026-08-07. An earlier version of this list stated that the R2 per-row cost was 'carried over from the E7b S8 per-row cost'. THAT WAS FALSE and is withdrawn: the E7b figure is S8_projection = 0.0291 MILLISECONDS for a LayerNorm-plus-Linear stage, a different operation in units 1000x apart. The same list also quoted an exposure of '+1.87 h, headroom about 0.17 h', which was computed on the superseded 7,714-row basis and the superseded headroom. Both figures are withdrawn. See open_risks for the current position, which this list must not contradict.

NEITHER the R2 nor the R3 per-row cost is measured for E8B, and neither has a source. Together they carry 1.214 h on the pretrained identity. At 3x the assumed rate the identity rises by 2.428 h and the 0.577 h headroom is EXHAUSTED.
the 250k training rate is step-scaled from the measured 40k rate; no 250k E8B cell has ever run. It carries about 12.7 h.

the G14 per-row cost is the pooled measurement 5.139 s plus a 3.15 per cent margin, and is OPTIMISTIC rather than conservative: the measurement covers the two R1 scorers only, while the live gate also runs both R2 walks per row.

A4 and A7c (3.668 h) are expected-epoch projections for arms that have not run; their configured 100-epoch cap would cost 8.469 h each. A1, the one arm of this family that has run, came in 23 per cent below its projection.
the retained parts of protocol 13.2b's A1 row (0.723 h) are that protocol's own estimates for work that has not run.
the section-19 efficiency pass is charged at the upper bound of its 0.500-1.000 h range.
B1 is charged at an upper bound and touches neither identity's 35-hour ceiling, though it does count toward the 180-hour core ceiling.

enforcement.previously: the 35 h per-identity ceiling and the storage gate existed only as constants and helper functions with no call site in the execution path, so neither could have halted anything. Nothing summed GPU hours across cells.
enforcement.now: run.per_identity_gate reads an append-only ledger (gpu_hour_ledger.json) and is checked BEFORE every core cell against that cell's projected cost, then re-checked AFTER the cell against its MEASURED hours, which are charged to the ledger. run.storage_gate is checked before every cell. Both halt through gate_halt.
enforcement.verified: the executable gate reproduces the published projection to within 0.003 h (33.4747 against 33.472, the difference being the rounded per-cell constants the gate uses), and fires above it.
